MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
D. REGISTER
B. D. 7038

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, MAY 15, 1936

Arrests Of British
Employees Aired

Commons Hears Report
On Japanese Action
In Manchuria

(Reuter's Agency)
LONDON, May 13—The reported arrest by "Manchukuo" police and Japanese gendarmerie of Chinese subjects employed by British firms and missionary societies in South Manchuria was the subject of questions in the House of Commons today by Mr. A. C. Morting, Conservative member for Preston.

In October and November last, declared the Prime Minister, Mr. Stanley Baldwin, in reply, a number of Chinese connected with British interests in South Manchuria were arrested on suspicion of having alleged Communist tendencies. No British subjects were arrested, but in view of the fact that in effecting the arrests British extra-territorial rights were infringed and general inconvenience was caused to British charitable and commercial institutions in South Manchuria, representations were made to the Japanese Government and the Manchurian authorities.

Afterwards, Mr. Baldwin declared, all but five prisoners were released.

Between April 14 and 17, however, further arrests were made on similar grounds, six of whom were connected with British firms or institutions.

The British Ambassador in Tokyo, Sir Robert Clive, the House was informed, had been instructed to make further representations to the Japanese Government.

《字林西报》，1936年5月15日，星期五

英国雇员被捕一事引发讨论

下议院听取关于日本在满洲行动的报告

（路透社）
伦敦，5月13日电——据报，“满洲国”警察和日本宪兵队逮捕了在南满受雇于英国公司和传教团体的中国籍人员，此事成为今日在下议院由保守党普雷斯顿选区议员A. C. Morting先生提出质询的主题。

首相斯坦利·鲍德温先生在答复中宣称，去年十月和十一月，南满与英国利益有关联的若干中国人因涉嫌具有所谓的共产主义倾向而被捕。没有英国臣民被捕，但鉴于在实施逮捕过程中侵犯了英国的治外法权，并给南满的英国慈善和商业机构造成了普遍的不便，已向日本政府和满洲当局提出了交涉。

随后，鲍德温先生宣布，除五名囚犯外，其余均获释。

然而，在4月14日至17日期间，又以类似理由进行了进一步逮捕，其中六人与英国公司或机构有关联。

据悉，已指示驻东京英国大使罗伯特·克莱夫爵士向日本政府作进一步交涉。

page_data.en:
Translation from the Russian newspaper "Novosty Dnia"
of October 30, 1935.

THE WAVE OF ARRESTS IN HARBIN

Arrested:- Kabalkin, Marianna Kolosova, Artist
Dalevich and many others.

The plundering newspaper "Nash Put" is closed
by the authorities.

During the last few days constant rumours are
circulating in town regarding happenings in Harbin of
rather a serious nature. According to these rumours,
which are confirmed from various sources, it is learned
that the Manchukuo authorities have closed down the
"fascist" paper of Rodzaevsky, the "Nash Put," published
in Harbin, and which had a scandalous reputation. Through
this paper common blackmail was carried out slightly
disguised by the "ideological" mask. At the time of the
closure of the paper, the owner of it, Rodzaevsky, was
subjected to repression, the nature of which is not yet
known. The poetess Marianna Kolosova, widely known for
her political work, was also arrested. Mention is also
made of the arrest of a well known merchant and factory
owner, Kabalkin, who is the assistant chairman of the
Exchange Committee and owner of the "Anglo-Chinese
Manufacturing Co." The reason for his arrest is not yet
known. Last night the local theater circles received
a letter from Harbin which states that L. Dalevich, an
artist well known in Shanghai, was arrested on October 12,
just on eve of his departure to the USSR. Dalevich
was accused of a rather serious crime, i.e. espionage for
one of the "neighbouring country." No details regarding
his arrest are given and no conclusion could be arrived at
at present as to what really happened there. Dalevich
at present is kept in the Harbin prison.

（批：See Q. 5835）

译自1935年10月30日俄文报纸《Novosty Dnia》。

哈尔滨的逮捕浪潮

被捕者：卡巴尔金（Kabalkin）、玛丽安娜·科洛索娃（Marianna Kolosova）、艺术家达列维奇（Dalevich）及许多人。

掠夺性报纸《我们的道路》（Nash Put）被当局查封。

近几日，市内不断流传着关于哈尔滨发生相当严重事件的谣言。根据这些得到多方证实的谣言获悉，满洲国当局已关闭了罗扎耶夫斯基（Rodzaevsky）在哈尔滨出版的、声名狼藉的法西斯报纸《我们的道路》。通过该报，以“意识形态”面具稍加掩饰的方式进行了普通的敲诈勒索。在该报被关闭时，其所有者罗扎耶夫斯基遭到镇压，其性质尚不清楚。以政治工作闻名的女诗人玛丽安娜·科洛索娃也被捕。还提到知名商人和工厂主卡巴尔金被捕，他是交易所委员会副主席兼“英华制造公司”（Anglo-Chinese Manufacturing Co.）的所有者。其被捕原因尚不清楚。昨晚，本地戏剧界收到一封来自哈尔滨的信，称在上海知名的艺术家L. 达列维奇于10月12日被捕，正值他启程前往苏联前夕。达列维奇被指控犯有相当严重的罪行，即为某一“邻国”从事间谍活动。关于其逮捕的细节未予提供，目前无法就那里实际发生的情况得出任何结论。达列维奇目前被关押在哈尔滨监狱。

（批注：见 Q. 5835）

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / REGISTRY / No. S. B. D. 7038 / Date 29th October 1935）

Subject Arrests in Mukden and Harbin.

Made by ............................................................ Forwarded by D. S. S. Byrne

On Oct. 22, 1935 there arrived in Shanghai from Harbin a
Mr. Ho Chun who was until recently employed in the Accounts
Department of the National City Bank of New York, Harbin Branch.
When interviewed by the undersigned on October 25, Mr. Ho stated
that he had been transferred to the Shanghai office of the Bank
at his own request, as he feared to remain in Harbin after an
experience which befell him at the end of August, 1935.
Questioned regarding this experience Mr. Ho related how,
on the morning of Aug. 28, a Japanese and two Chinese detectives
called at the Bank and stated that he was wanted at Police Head-
quarters. In spite of the remonstrances of the Manager of the
Bank he was taken away and lodged in a cell at the Police
Station, where he remained for three days. During this period
he was not interrogated, nor was any reason given for his
detention. After his release he learned that approximately
5,000 persons had been taken into custody, the reason being,-
according to an official statement made some time later - that
all suspected reactionaries would be placed under preventative
detention during the visit of Emperor Pu Yih to Harbin.
Continuing, Mr. Ho related how, during the past two
months, the arrest of employees of Foreign establishment had
been a daily occurrence, the arrests in many cases being effect-
ed on the premises of firms enjoying Consular protection. In
the earlier cases protests were lodged by the Consuls of the
nationals concerned, but as it was found that in such instances
the arrested persons were kept in custody longer than usual,
it was found expedient to make no protest, but await the
release of the arrested person. The Japanese Authorities,
with whom the protests were lodged, usually denied having

主题 沈阳和哈尔滨的逮捕事件。

制作人 ............................................................ 转呈人 D. S. S. Byrne

1935年10月22日，一位何春（Ho Chun，音译）先生从哈尔滨抵达上海，他最近一直在纽约花旗银行哈尔滨分行会计部任职。10月25日接受卑职问询时，何先生表示，由于害怕留在哈尔滨，他在1935年8月底经历了一次事件后，主动要求调往该银行上海办事处。当被问及这次经历时，何先生叙述道，8月28日上午，一名日本人和两名中国侦探来到银行，声称警察总局要见他。尽管银行经理提出抗议，他仍被带走并关押在警察局的牢房里，在那里待了三天。在此期间，他未受审讯，也未被告知拘留理由。获释后他得知，约有5,000人被拘捕，据后来的一份官方声明称，原因是——在溥仪皇帝访问哈尔滨期间，所有嫌疑反动分子都将被预防性拘留。
何先生接着叙述，在过去两个月里，外国机构雇员的逮捕已成为日常现象，在许多情况下，逮捕是在享有领事保护的公司场所内执行的。在早期的案件中，相关国籍的领事提出了抗议，但由于发现此类情况下被捕人员的拘留时间比平时更长，因此认为不提出抗议、等待被捕人员获释更为适宜。日本当局（抗议对象）通常否认

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, OCTOBER 22, 1935

SENSATIONAL MUKDEN ARRESTS

Employees of British Concerns Taken Into
Custody: Huge Building Programme

FROM OUR OWN CORRESPONDENT

Mukden, Oct. 16.
Beginning on October 11 there occurred a series of arrests which has caused a brief sensation in Mukden. Those involved include; a foreign-educated doctor in the old city; a Chinese, Christian pastor, prominent in Y.M.C.A. work; Chinese employees of the Chi Tung Tobacco Co., Manchurian subsidiary of the B.A.T. Co.; five doctors, two male nurses and one technician from the Mukden Hospital, Missionary medical centre whose great work for the people of this district has long been recognized as an outstanding example of British missionary effort; the assistant comprador of the Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corporation; teachers in the middle school, maintained by British missions; two Chinese from the British Cigarette Company's Mukden factory; pupils from a mission school for girls, and the steward from the International Golf Club. A very mixed bag was the first comment heard on Saturday.

But it seemed perplexing that the Chinese taken were all connected with British firms and organizations nor was the explanation that British interests greatly outnumbered those of other nationalities found acceptable. In some instances permission was sought by the police for the entering of British property but at least two instances are reported where flagrant violation of private rights were apparently committed. A foreign bachelors' mess on premises long owned by a British concern were entered and searched, and very late on the night of Sunday, October 13, the police are reported to have forced their way into British premises and there arrested a girl student in the mission school. Enquiries at H. M. Consulate-General indicated that no permission had been sought for this entrance into British property.

No Official Statement
Official statements as to the cause of these raids are not available and Japanese authorities when questioned professed entire ignorance of the matter, but Japanese in the employ of the Manchoukuo police are understood to have stated, to interested foreign authorities, that the gendarmes were in charge of the whole affair and would not permit any information to be given out. Brief paragraphs appeared in the local vernacular press but beyond indicating that police activities in connection with a "Certain serious affair" had caused a local sensation no information was given. In the absence of precise information rumours galore circulated throughout the town. A gigantic Communist plot was seen, but it was difficult to visualize some of the well-to-do local residents involved in the arrests as wholehearted exponents of Communistic principles.

For sometime an undefined relation to British interests seemed the only feature which the different arrests possessed in common. Then it was suggested that membership in, or at least a contribution to, the Y.M.C.A. or Y.W.C.A. seemed a link between the various persons affected. It was rumoured that many more arrests were taking place, and it was known that the police were working from a list which apparently they believed named persons connected with subversive activities, against the Manchoukuo Government. Rumour named 400 arrests and accounts of activities in Harbin began to be confused with reports in Mukden.

Another suggestion was that the police had found on the person some Chinese traveller from the south a mailing list which had been prepared by an industrious source of anti-Manchoukuo propaganda safely located in the South. The Chi Tung Tobacco Co. suffered no little inconvenience because of the sudden removal of so many of the senior employees in their accounting department. H.M. Consulate-General made every effort to minimize the inconvenience which must be felt by British concerns because of long absence of important members of their staffs, as well as endeavouring to insure that the property rights of British Subjects were respected.

Reg.
Please file
carefully. M
28 OCT. 1935

《字林西报》，1935年10月22日，星期二

沈阳逮捕案轰动一时

英国机构雇员被拘：庞大的建筑计划

本报特约记者

沈阳，10月16日电。
从10月11日开始，发生了一系列逮捕事件，在沈阳引起了短暂的轰动。涉案人员包括：老城区一名受过外国教育的医生；一名在基督教青年会工作中颇有声望的中国基督教牧师；英美烟草公司满洲子公司——启东烟草公司的中国雇员；来自沈阳医院（一家传教士医疗中心，其为该地区人民所做的巨大工作长期以来被视为英国传教努力的杰出典范）的五名医生、两名男护士和一名技术员；汇丰银行的助理买办；由英国传教团维持的中学的教师；英国卷烟公司沈阳工厂的两名中国人；一所教会女子学校的学生，以及国际高尔夫俱乐部的服务员。“真是鱼龙混杂”，这是周六听到的第一句评论。

但令人困惑的是，被捕的中国人均与英国公司和组织有关联，而“英国利益远远超过其他国籍”这一解释并未被接受。在某些情况下，警方寻求进入英国物业的许可，但据报道，至少有两起公然侵犯私权的案件显然发生了。警方进入并搜查了一处由英国公司长期拥有的外籍单身宿舍，据报道，在10月13日星期日深夜，警方强行闯入英国物业，并在那里逮捕了一名教会学校的女学生。向英国总领事馆查询表明，此次进入英国物业并未寻求许可。

无官方声明
关于这些突袭原因的官方声明尚未发布，日本当局在被问及时声称对此事完全不知情，但据了解，受雇于满洲国警察的日本人已向有关的外国当局表示，宪兵队负责整个事件，并且不允许发布任何信息。当地中文报刊刊登了简短段落，但除了指出与“某起严重事件”有关的警察活动引起了当地轰动外，未提供其他信息。由于缺乏确切信息，各种谣言在全城流传。有人看到了一个巨大的共产主义阴谋，但很难想象一些卷入逮捕案的当地富裕居民会是共产主义原则的全心全意拥护者。

一段时间以来，与英国利益存在某种未定义的关系似乎是不同逮捕案唯一的共同特征。随后有人提出，加入或至少向基督教青年会或基督教女青年会捐款，似乎是受影响的各种人员之间的联系纽带。谣传还有更多逮捕正在进行，且已知警方正依据一份名单开展工作，该名单显然列出了他们相信与颠覆满洲国政府活动有关的人员。谣言称有400人被捕，关于哈尔滨活动的报道开始与沈阳的报道混淆。

另一种说法是，警方在一名来自南方的中国旅客身上发现了一份邮寄名单，该名单由位于南方的一个积极的反满洲国宣传来源编制。由于会计部门众多高级雇员突然被带走，启东烟草公司遭受了不少不便。英国总领事馆尽一切努力尽量减少因重要职员长期缺席而给英国公司带来的不便，并努力确保英国臣民的财产权得到尊重。

Reg.
请仔细归档。 M
1935年10月28日

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 19, 1935

MANY ARRESTS IN
HARBIN

Elements Subversive to
Government

FROM OUR OWN CORRESPONDENT

Harbin, Oct. 9.
According to the local Russian
press, about 120 persons were
arrested yesterday, these including
the editor of the "Novosti Vostoka,"
the Soviet daily newspaper. Besides
the editor, other leading members of
the staff were arrested, thus making
it impossible for the paper to appear this morning. The Russian
press in commenting on the arrests,
states that it is necessary for the
peace and order of the city that all
injurious elements should be removed
and that such a "clean-up" will
be for the good of the entire
population. They are accused of
being connected with anti-Government elements, and also have the
support of a certain neighbouring
country. Rumours go the length of
stating that Russian emigrants will
be forbidden to reside in Manchoukuo. It is easily seen to what an
extent these rumours are false.
Their absurdity is proved by the
Russian emigrants themselves, who
residing in Manchoukuo, have the
rights of citizenship and the authorities far from persecuting in any way,
on the contrary, give them every
facility.
The Russian in Manchoukuo has
rights as the Russian residing in
Shanghai never dreamed of. The
government of Manchoukuo has built
up its state policy on high principles
of justice, never in any way persecuting its loyal citizens, no matter what their nationality.
On the other hand, ensuring peace
and order, the Government is taking measures to sift out harmful
elements from Manchoukuo. The
Government firmly has resolved to
remove from its country all persons
who are inclined to be hostile to
the principles which are the basis of
policy of Manchoukuo. The recent
arrests were for the purpose of removing such elements.

S2,
Please comment on
political significance of
these happenings. JAS
22 OCT. 1935

据当地俄文报刊报道，昨日约有120人被捕，其中包括苏联日报《东方新闻》（Novosti Vostoka）的编辑。除该编辑外，报社其他主要成员亦被捕，致使该报今晨无法出版。俄文报刊在评论此次逮捕行动时指出，为了城市的和平与秩序，必须清除所有有害分子，此类“清洗”将有利于全体居民。这些人被指控与反政府分子有联系，并得到某一邻国的支持。甚至有谣言称，俄国侨民将被禁止居住在满洲国。这些谣言的虚假程度显而易见。其荒谬性已由居住在满洲国的俄国侨民自身所证实，他们拥有公民权，当局非但没有以任何方式进行迫害，反而为他们提供各种便利。

在满洲国的俄国人所享有的权利，是居住在上海的俄国人从未梦想过的。满洲国政府基于崇高的正义原则建立其国家政策，从不以任何方式迫害其忠诚的公民，无论其国籍如何。

另一方面，为确保和平与秩序，政府正采取措施从满洲国筛除有害分子。政府已坚决决定将所有倾向于敌视构成满洲国政策基础之原则的人员驱逐出境。最近的逮捕行动旨在清除此类分子。
